walkthroughs.body_html: Stars above about 25 solar masses collapse into stellar-mass black holes, typically 5-30 solar masses. The most massive single stars may collapse directly without a bright supernova.
If a black hole has a normal companion, infalling gas forms a hot accretion disk radiating X-rays. Cygnus X-1 (identified in the 1970s) was the first strong stellar-mass candidate.
Pairs of stellar-mass black holes can inspiral and merge. LIGO's first detection (GW150914, 2015) involved 36 and 29 solar mass black holes — confirming the class observationally.
